metadata.file_name: 43. Hu et al. (2025). Predicting adolescents’ environmental action: From individual to national-level factors using an explainable machine learning approach.pdf
metadata.title: Predicting adolescents’ environmental action: From individual to national-level factors using an explainable machine learning approach

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata with a two-stage stratified probability-proportional-to-size design: schools are sampled first, then up to 42 students are sampled within each school. The authors report PISA international response-rate targets at the school (85%, weighted) and student (80%, weighted) levels and state that systems failing to meet thresholds were excluded from the public database, supporting national representativeness within participating countries. In the machine-learning pipeline, the manuscript does not explicitly state whether PISA sampling weights (e.g., student-level or school-level weights) were applied during model training/evaluation; therefore, weight usage is not documented at the analysis stage. The authors do report standard ML preprocessing steps (train/test split, MICE-based predictive mean matching imputation, and SMOTE oversampling) and use SHAP for post-hoc interpretation, but these steps are described without a clear linkage to complex-survey weighting.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variables are private- and public-sphere environmental actions, which are behavioral/action items rather than PISA cognitive achievement scales with Plausible Values; thus PV handling is not applicable to the modeled outcomes. However, the manuscript does not explicitly confirm whether any PV-based constructs were included among predictors or outcomes, so PV handling is treated as not reported for transparency. Missing data handling is documented via MICE predictive mean matching, but PV-specific documentation is absent because the modeled targets are not PV-based achievement scores.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 for adolescents aged 15 (PISA target population). The analytic sample was restricted to adolescents who answered the environmental-action items; cases who did not answer the environmental-action items were excluded. The final sample comprises 420,339 adolescents from 66 countries. For ML modeling, the dataset was further split into training (90%) and testing (10%) sets, with stratified 10-fold cross-validation applied within the training set.

main_findings.performance_metrics: LightGBM (validation): Accuracy 0.699, F1 0.698, Recall 0.699, AUC 0.762. LightGBM (test): Accuracy 0.700, F1 0.702, Recall 0.702, AUC 0.767. XGBoost selected for private-sphere actions (test): Accuracy/Recall 0.833, AUC 0.718; Random Forest highest F1 (0.781 vs 0.772 for LightGBM).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 the study leveraged environmental attitude, critical thinking, climate-change explanatory capacity, sense of life meaning, and school belonging to predict private-sphere environmental actions, finding that individual and school factors were the most influential and that model performance was stronger for private-sphere than public-sphere actions. This indicates that strengthening adolescents’ climate-related knowledge and personal attitudes—supported by school environments that build belonging and supportive discussion—may be an effective pathway for promoting household environmental behaviors, though the cross-sectional design prevents causal claims.

main_findings.performance_metrics: LightGBM (validation): Accuracy 0.699, F1 0.698, Recall 0.699, AUC 0.762. LightGBM (test): Accuracy 0.700, F1 0.702, Recall 0.702, AUC 0.767. XGBoost (validation): Accuracy 0.830, Recall 0.830, AUC 0.709; Random Forest highest F1 0.780. XGBoost (test): Accuracy/Recall 0.833, AUC 0.718; Random Forest slightly higher F1 (0.781 vs 0.772).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 the study leveraged environmental attitude, international event discussion, school belonging, mean sustainable development score, and environmental performance index to predict public-sphere environmental actions, finding that public actions were jointly shaped by individual, school, and national factors and that national context variables ranked highly in SHAP importance. This indicates that education policy should pair school-level civic/participation supports with national sustainability commitments and governance signals to better enable adolescents’ collective environmental engagement, while recognizing that SHAP-based importance reflects prediction contribution rather than causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata from 66 countries (final analytic sample: 420,339 adolescents) to predict two types of adolescent environmental action: private-sphere and public-sphere behaviors. After excluding students who did not answer the environmental-action items, the authors train four ML classifiers (LightGBM, XGBoost, Random Forest, and an MLP) using a 90/10 train-test split and stratified 10-fold cross-validation with Optuna hyperparameter tuning. Missing values are imputed using MICE predictive mean matching, and class imbalance is addressed with SMOTE. For public-sphere actions, LightGBM achieved the best reported performance on validation/test (Accuracy ≈0.699–0.700; F1 ≈0.698–0.702; AUC ≈0.762–0.767). For private-sphere actions, XGBoost showed the highest accuracy/recall on the test set (Accuracy/Recall 0.833; AUC 0.718), while Random Forest slightly led F1. SHAP is used for interpretability, but the paper notes cross-sectional limitations, and the manuscript does not clearly document whether PISA sampling weights were applied during ML training/evaluation.
